meta.title: Engram · Study your flashcards out loud
meta.description: Android app that studies your flashcards with you by voice. A tutor reads each card, listens to your answer and grades what you meant. Works with AnkiDroid decks, decks you make in Engram, or decks written by AI from your notes.

hero.kicker: A voice tutor for your flashcards · Android
hero.title: Study your flashcards out loud.
hero.lede: Engram reads you a card and listens to your answer. Say it your way: it checks what you meant, not the exact words. Your phone can stay in your pocket.
hero.hint: Android 7 or newer · Works with AnkiDroid, or on its own

manifesto.title: No hearts to lose. No streak to break.
manifesto.body: Cards you know go to your pile. Cards you miss go back under the deck and come round again. That's the whole game.

session.title: Every card goes the same way.
session.lede: Pick a deck, put your headphones on, and the session runs by voice. No need to look at the screen.

steps.title: Archie asks
steps.body: The question is read out loud, in the language you set for that deck.

steps.title: You answer
steps.body: Out loud, in your own words. The back of the card shows up on screen as soon as you finish.

steps.title: Engram grades
steps.body: Your answer is checked against the card. A synonym or a different order is fine. A missing fact is not.

steps.title: You hear why
steps.body: Miss it and you hear the right answer. Then the next card is dealt.

session.commandsTitle: Talk to it like a person.
session.commandsLede: Any wording works, in any language. Some things you can say:

commands.does: Hear the answer and move on.
Move on. The card comes back later.
Change the grade of the card you just answered.
It stops coming up until you fix it.
End the session with a short summary.

decks.title: Bring your decks, or make new ones.
decks.lede: Engram studies any deck you point it at. You don't need AnkiDroid to start.

items.title: Your AnkiDroid decks
items.body: Engram reads them through AnkiDroid's official API and writes each grade back as Good or Again, as if you had tapped it. Your cards, note types and deck options stay as they are.

items.title: Decks you make in Engram
items.body: No AnkiDroid? Make decks right in the app and add cards by hand. A built-in scheduler brings each card back when it's due.

items.title: Decks written from your notes
items.body: Say what you want to learn, or attach notes: PDF, slides, Word files or photos. Archie asks a few questions, writes the cards and sets up the tutor. You check every card before saving.

archie.title: Meet Archie.
body: Archie is a filing cabinet. He deals the cards, keeps the ones you miss in play, and when the session ends he files them away until they're due again.
If you want, he'll remind you to study: at most once a day, and only when cards are waiting. Skip a day and nothing breaks.
archie.tablesLede: Three themes, each with a day side and a night side. Engram follows your phone's dark mode. Try them on this page:

items.title: Any subject, any language
items.body: Medicine, code, languages, law, cloud certifications. Set the tutor's language per deck: Spanish cards in Spanish, Japanese cards in Japanese.

items.title: Grading you control
items.body: Gist, Standard or Precise, per deck. Add your own instructions for the tutor, like "be strict with technical terms".

items.title: Screen off, hands free
items.body: The session keeps going with the screen off: on a walk, doing the dishes, at the gym. Never while driving.

items.title: Your audio stays off our servers
items.body: Your voice goes from your phone straight to OpenAI's realtime model. We don't store or relay audio.

pricing.title: Priced by the minute of voice.
pricing.lede: Each minute of voice costs us money to run, so plans are counted in minutes. Paused time doesn't count.

items.question: Do I need AnkiDroid?
items.answer: No. You can make decks in Engram, or have Archie write one from your notes. If you already use AnkiDroid, Engram can study those decks too.

items.question: Does it change my Anki collection?
items.answer: Only the grades. Engram reads your cards through AnkiDroid's official API and writes each result back as Good or Again, as if you had tapped it. Cards, note types and deck options stay as they are.

items.question: What if it grades me wrong?
items.answer: Say "I was right" and the card you just answered is marked correct. "That was wrong" works the other way.

items.question: Does it mess up my review schedule?
items.answer: No. A grade from Engram is an ordinary review, and your scheduler handles it like any other.

items.question: Where does my voice go?
items.answer: From your phone straight to OpenAI's realtime model, which hears you and speaks the tutor's replies. The text of your answer goes to TypeSafe (Jev), which grades it. We never store your audio.

items.question: Does it work offline?
items.answer: No. The tutor runs online, so a session needs a connection.

items.question: Is there an iPhone version?
items.answer: Not yet. Engram is Android only for now.

items.question: Can I use it while driving?
items.answer: No. Not in a car, on a motorbike or on a bike. Use it walking, cooking, doing the dishes or at the gym, where a moment of distraction is harmless.

items.question: Why are there minute limits?
items.answer: Every minute of voice costs us money with the AI provider. Counting minutes keeps the price fixed and tells you exactly what you're paying for.
